text:
Arjun Patel: Pushed an nsys trace from today's load test — tail latency spikes when prefix reuse goes >85%. Trace uploaded: s3://redwood-traces/eng-runtime/2065432100-nsys.qd. Quick skim: timeline shows a long gap around kernel launches and repeated `fallback_gemm` kernels leading into a burst of cudaMemcpy stalls.

Maria Gomez: hmm can you paste the kernel timeline snippet? do we see kernelselect flipping between variants?

Arjun Patel: pasted snippet from the nsys summary: 
```
Kernel timeline (nsys):
0ms   - attention_kv_lookup (fast)
+3ms  - prefer_fp16_matmul (fast)
+11ms - fallback_gemm (2.3ms)
+15ms - cudaMemcpy (host->dev) (blocked 8ms)
```
Memory copies right after small-sequence kernels look suspicious — copies are blocking other streams.

Kate Lin: Did we recently flip the 'prefer_large_gemm' heuristic in kernelselect? that could pick a slower large-GEMM path for short seq lengths and cause memcpy boundaries.

PerfBot: Regression detected: commit c3f5b24 toggled kernelselect:prefer_large_gemm=true. Observed +18% 95th latency on synthetic load tests.

Luis Ortega: On the trace the prefix KV hit rate dips right before the spikes (we have nvtx ranges around cache lookup). Looks like eviction policy thrash when batch sizes merge. When a few large batches coalesce, KV entries get evicted then re-populated, causing prefix misses and extra matmuls.

Samira Chen: Repro steps I ran locally: 
```
./tools/load_test --model redwood-63B --seq 2048 --concurrency 48 --warmup 2000 --duration 600
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace_2065432100 --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=cpu
```
I can repro the 95th spike ~70s into the run.

Maria Gomez: Can we try overriding kernelselect to prefer_small_gemm for seq < 512? also temporarily cap batch merging to 40 to avoid eviction bursts.

Arjun Patel: quick experiment: override -> prefer_small_gemm for short seqs; 95th drops ~9%, KV hitstability improves. Throughput drops ~6% in peak, so it's a latency vs throughput tradeoff.

Kate Lin: sounds like expected tradeoff. For production we should A/B with a small traffic split and monitor token/sec. If latency win justifies cost, we can keep it.

Luis Ortega: smaller mitigation idea: increase cache eviction grace window from 120ms -> 300ms so entries aren't evicted during transient batch spikes. That should raise KV hits without forcing gemm change.

Samira Chen: I'll run a perfetto capture focused on cpu stacks during the memcpy stalls and NVTX ranges for cache ops, then upload link. Command I'll run: 
```
python tools/perfetto_capture.py --pid $(pgrep runtime) --duration 60 --out /tmp/perfetto_2065432100.pb
```

Arjun Patel: thanks. TODOs I added: 1) run perfetto capture (nvtx + cpu), 2) A/B kernelselect flags for small seqs, 3) change eviction grace -> 300ms and run quick smoke, 4) re-run load test and compare 95/99th and KV hit rate. assigning @Kate Lin and @Luis Ortega to follow up.

Kate Lin: ack :thumbsup:

PerfBot: New perfetto trace available: https://perfetto.local/trace/2065432100 (nvtx + cpu stacks)

Maria Gomez: Nice thread. If someone gets a consistent repro, let's sync EOD in eng-runtime standup and decide whether to revert kernelselect commit or ship eviction-window change first.
